sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s explore how to use Java’s built-in math tools to make calculations easier! No need to reinvent the wheel—Java’s `Math` class has you covered.

• How to use `Math.pow()` for exponents (like 2³)
• Why the `Math` class is your math buddy
• Common math operations you’ll use daily

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re baking a cake. Instead of measuring ingredients from scratch, you use pre-measured cups—saves time, right? The `Math` class is like those pre-measured cups for programming!

Java’s `Math` class gives you ready-to-use methods for common calculations. No need to write complex logic for exponents, square roots, or rounding—just call a method!

• **Exponents**: `Math.pow(a, b)` calculates `a` raised to the power of `b` (e.g., `2³ = 8`)
• **Precision**: Works with `double` values (e.g., `Math.pow(4, 0.5) = 2.0`)
• **Easy to use**: Just write `Math.pow(base, exponent)`—no extra setup needed!

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
System.out.println(Math.abs(-4.5));    // 4.5
System.out.println(Math.sqrt(16));     // 4.0
System.out.println(Math.pow(2, 10));   // 1024.0
System.out.println(Math.max(3, 7));    // 7
System.out.println(Math.min(3, 7));    // 3
System.out.println(Math.round(3.6));   // 4
System.out.println(Math.ceil(3.1));    // 4.0
System.out.println(Math.floor(3.9));   // 3.0

sections.title: Key Points
points: Math.abs() returns the absolute value; Math.sqrt() returns the square root
Math.pow(a, b) returns a raised to the power of b
Math.max() and Math.min() return the larger and smaller of two values
Math.round() rounds to the nearest integer; Math.ceil() rounds up; Math.floor() rounds down
Math.random() returns a random double between 0.0 (inclusive) and 1.0 (exclusive)

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `Math.pow(a, b)` is your go-to for exponents—no loops needed. Always returns a `double` (e.g., `8.0` instead of `8`) Practice with real-world formulas (like circle area or compound interest)

questions.question: What does Math.pow(2, 3) return?
questions.explanation: Math.pow(2, 3) computes 2 raised to the power of 3, which is 2 * 2 * 2 = 8.0. The method returns a double value.

questions.question: What does Math.sqrt(16) return?
questions.explanation: Math.sqrt(16) returns the square root of 16, which is 4.0. The method always returns a double value.
